steps.title: Create the Timer component
steps.instructions: Create a React app with npx create-react-app demo-app, then start the dev server with npm start. Add src/Components/Timer.js with a seconds state and a useEffect that runs setInterval every 1000ms.

targets.caption: Start the interval inside useEffect with an empty dependency array

explanations.topic: Why cleanup prevents memory leaks and unwanted side effects
Timer component state and setInterval logic

hints: Which React hooks do you need to track seconds and start an interval on mount?
Pass an empty dependency array [] to useEffect so the interval is created once on mount.
Use setSeconds(prevSeconds => prevSeconds + 1) inside setInterval(..., 1000) and export Timer as default.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the empty dependency array [] on useEffect, causing a new interval on every render
Using seconds + 1 instead of the functional updater prevSeconds => prevSeconds + 1
Forgetting export default Timer at the bottom of Timer.js
steps.code:
import React, { useEffect, useState } from 'react'; function Timer() { const [seconds, setSeconds] = useState(0); useEffect(() => { setInterval(() => { setSeconds(prevSeconds => prevSeconds + 1); console.log('timer running...'); }, 1000); }, []); return (
seconds : {seconds}
); } export default Timer;

steps.title: Toggle Timer in App component
steps.instructions: In src/App.js, import Timer, add a boolean showTimer state initialized to false, and render a Toggle Timer button alongside {showTimer && <Timer/>}. Toggle the timer on and off in Chrome and watch the console keep logging after unmount.

targets.caption: Conditionally mount and unmount Timer based on showTimer

explanations.topic: Using conditional rendering to mount and unmount Timer
Why the unmounted timer keeps logging without cleanup

hints: How can you conditionally render <Timer/> in JSX using a boolean state?
Create const [showTimer, setShowTimer] = useState(false) and toggle it in the button onClick handler.
common_mistakes: Passing setShowTimer(!showTimer) directly to onClick instead of wrapping it in an arrow function () => setShowTimer(!showTimer)
steps.code:
import React, { useState } from "react"; import Timer from "./Components/Timer"; function App() { const [showTimer, setShowTimer] = useState(false); return (
{showTimer && }
); } export default App;

steps.title: Return cleanup function in Timer
steps.instructions: In src/Components/Timer.js, store setInterval's return value in intervalId and return a cleanup function from useEffect that calls clearInterval(intervalId) and logs 'clean up called'. Run npm start and toggle Timer off in Chrome to verify the timer stops.

targets.caption: Return a cleanup function from useEffect to clear the interval on unmount

explanations.topic: Returning a cleanup function with clearInterval from useEffect
Verifying cleanup stops the background timer on unmount

hints: What does setInterval return so you can cancel it later?
Assign const intervalId = setInterval(...) and return () => { ... } at the end of the useEffect callback.
Inside the returned cleanup function, call clearInterval(intervalId) and console.log('clean up called').
common_mistakes: Calling clearInterval(intervalId) directly inside useEffect instead of inside a returned function
Forgetting to save the interval ID returned by setInterval
steps.code: const intervalId = setInterval(() => { setSeconds(prevSeconds => prevSeconds + 1); console.log('timer running...'); }, 1000); return () => { clearInterval(intervalId); console.log('clean up called'); };

steps.title: Run cleanup on state change
steps.instructions: In src/Components/Timer.js, add a reset boolean state with a Reset button, include reset in the useEffect dependency array, and call setSeconds(0) inside the cleanup. Click Reset in Chrome to verify cleanup runs and seconds restart from 0.

targets.caption: Reset seconds in cleanup, which runs whenever the dependency changes

explanations.topic: How cleanup executes before re-running useEffect when a dependency changes
Tracing Reset button state change through cleanup and new interval creation

hints: How do you make useEffect re-run when the user clicks a Reset button?
Add const [reset, setReset] = useState(false) and put [reset] as the dependency array of useEffect.
Call setSeconds(0) inside the cleanup function and toggle reset in <button onClick={() => setReset(!reset)}>Reset</button>.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to add reset to the useEffect dependency array [reset], so clicking Reset never triggers cleanup
Wrapping multiple JSX elements in Timer return without a parent <div>
steps.code:
const [reset, setReset] = useState(false); useEffect(() => { const intervalId = setInterval(() => { setSeconds(prevSeconds => prevSeconds + 1); console.log('timer running...'); }, 1000); return () => { clearInterval(intervalId); setSeconds(0); console.log('clean up called'); }; }, [reset]); return (
seconds : {seconds}
);
